chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'The stoning (rajm) is not obligated until the four testimonies (bayyinah) are established — that they have seen him copulating with her.'

key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: Rajm — stoning as a legal punishment (hadd) for proven adultery in Islamic law
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ الْأَرْبَعَةُ: Al-bayyinah al-arba'ah — the four testimonies/witnesses required as proof for adultery
key_terms.يَجِبُ: Yajib — is obligated/required; a technical term in Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh) denoting legal obligation
key_terms.يُجَامِعُهَا: Yujami'uha — copulating with her; the explicit visual testimony required of all four witnesses

ai.seo_question: How many witnesses are required to establish stoning punishment for adultery in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes one of the most stringent evidentiary requirements in Islamic criminal law: stoning for adultery (zina) is not applicable unless four witnesses testify that they directly observed the act of intercourse. This extremely high threshold of proof — practically impossible to meet by chance — reflects the Islamic legal tradition's intent to make this punishment exceedingly rare in practice while preserving its deterrent function. The ruling is consistent with the Quranic standard of four witnesses for the accusation of adultery (24:4, 24:13).
